# 2 Baruch Chapter 7 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 7:2 — "was given leave" vs. "was permitted"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "was-given-leave to-go-with-the-captives" | Literal idiomatic compound |
| LOGOS | "was given leave to go with the captives" | Formal English idiom |
| PNEUMA | "was permitted to go with the captives" | Simplified single verb |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Given leave" retains the sense of formal permission granted by an authority (the Babylonian commander or God), whereas "permitted" is more casual.

---

## 7:2 — "remained there" vs. "stayed behind"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "but-I-Baruch remained-there" | Literal, first-person emphatic |
| LOGOS | "but I Baruch remained there" | Formal, preserves first-person emphasis |
| PNEUMA | "But I, Baruch, stayed behind" | "Stayed behind" is colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Remained there" is weightier — it signals deliberate witness, not mere absence. PNEUMA's "stayed behind" sounds passive rather than purposeful.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 2**
